# Connected reductive groups over infinite fields are generated by finitely many tori

Author: Worker 947.

`Langlands.GroupScheme.reductiveFiniteTorusGeneration` proves exactly the
published proposition
`Langlands.GroupScheme.ReductiveFiniteTorusGenerationStatement.{u}` from
`Reductive/TorusGenerationStatement.lean`, at arbitrary universe `u`, with no
outer hypotheses. For every infinite field `k : Type u` and every group scheme
`G` over `Spec k` with `IsConnectedReductive G`, it gives a natural number `m`,
tori `T j` (`j : Fin m`) and closed subgroup inclusions `ι j : T j ⟶ G`. Every
closed subgroup `i : H ⟶ G` through which all `ι j` factor has
`SubgroupFunctor.range i = ⊤` on every test scheme. Imperfect infinite fields,
every characteristic, nonsplit groups and the trivial group (where `m = 0` is
allowed) are all covered. The statement pair and everything it imports are
unchanged.

## Implemented proof

The proof is a single term that composes published Library theorems:

1. `reductiveFiniteTorusGeneration_of_cartanGeneration`
   (`Cartan/FiniteGeneration.lean`) derives the target from two premises,
   `CartanGenerationStatement.{u}` and `MaximalTorusCentralizerStatement.{u}`.
   It takes the family of all Cartan subgroups of `G`. The centralizer premise
   makes each of them a closed torus. The Cartan-generation premise makes the
   family generate `G`. The published generic dimension argument
   `FiniteGeneration.exists_finite_generating_subfamily_of_pointedImageGeneration`
   then selects a finite generating subfamily, and the adapter reindexes it by
   `Fin m`.
2. The first premise is `cartanGenerationStatement`
   (`Cartan/GenerationProof.lean`), the published unconditional proof of
   Cartan generation over infinite fields.
3. The second premise is
   `maximalTorusCentralizer_of_structuralInputs dynamicCentralizerReductive
   noTorusUnipotent solvableTorusQuotient`.
   `maximalTorusCentralizer_of_structuralInputs`
   (`Absolute/AlgClosedMaximalTorusCentralizerAssembly.lean`) derives
   `MaximalTorusCentralizerStatement.{u}` from three structural statements.
   Each one is supplied by its published unconditional proof:
   - `dynamicCentralizerReductive` (`Dynamic/CentralizerReductiveProof.lean`)
     proves `DynamicCentralizerReductiveStatement.{u}`;
   - `noTorusUnipotent` (`Torus/NoTorusUnipotent.lean`) proves
     `NoTorusUnipotentStatement.{u}`;
   - `solvableTorusQuotient` (`Absolute/SolvableTorusQuotientProof.lean`)
     proves `SolvableTorusQuotientStatement.{u}`.

All five theorems are stated at the same arbitrary universe `u`, so the
composite has exactly the target type and no structural premise remains.
The same composition for the centralizer statement appears as the separate
candidate `maximalTorusCentralizer` on task `acbc801a`. That candidate was
not yet published when this proof was written, so it is not imported here.

The import closure does not contain
`Langlands.GroupScheme.ReductiveTorusDominationStatement` or
`Langlands.GroupScheme.ReductiveRationalPointDensityStatement`, nor any
module that uses either of them. Both are downstream consumers of this result.

## Provenance

This module is internal: it composes published Library proofs and adds no new
mathematics. The source argument is that of the statement Markdown
`Reductive/TorusGenerationStatement.md`: Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017),
source ID `milne-2017-algebraic-groups`, Theorem 17.91 (printed p.381, PDF
p.397), which says a connected group variety over an infinite field is
generated by its Cartan subgroups, together with Corollary 17.84 (printed
p.379, PDF p.395), which says a maximal torus of a connected reductive group
is its own centralizer. The finite subfamily comes from the dimension
argument of Propositions 2.50 and 2.53. The Lean route proves 17.84 through
the published structural assembly listed above. That route is a derived
alternative to Milne's proof, and its own Markdown documents it. Worker 1342
authored the adapter, Workers 1296 and 1377 the Cartan generation proof, and
Worker 303 the centralizer assembly. The authors of the three structural
proofs are named in their own Markdown files.
